clue.text: Could be Mira, twinkling star taken from a city in India

indicators.note: a twinkling star flickers and shifts, so the letters before it are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; Mira is a real star
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer muses that the star Mira could be seen twinkling over an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the letters of the city, rearranged, could be Mira and star. AMRITSAR is a city in Punjab.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in the Punjab region of northern India, home of the Golden Temple.

clue.text: 50 introduced to remakably special food flavouring

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published has the typo 'remakably' for 'remarkably'; it doesn't change the parse. ALLSPICE is SPECIAL plus L, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is a spice from dried pimento berries, used to season food.

clue.text: Reasonable grounds detailed

blocks.note: a rationale is the grounds or reasons for something

explanation.surface: Someone sets out sensible reasons in full detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'set out at length' but is read as de-tailed: RATIONALE loses its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational and reasonable are synonyms, both describing thinking that is sensible and logical.

clue.text: Curt, in sister's estimation

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: In a sibling's opinion, someone is being curt.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt and terse are synonyms, both meaning rudely brief in speech.

clue.text: Very good, or very bad?

explanation.definitionFit: Wicked means evil in standard use but excellent in informal slang, a pair of opposite senses.

clue.text: Lover from Ontario, possibly coming round in the morning

clue.text: Christopher, 10, leads one to new-born pet?

blocks.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher
the number written as a word

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example rather than a strict synonym: a young cat is one kind of new pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a very young cat, often a newly acquired household pet.

clue.text: County Down's top store bombed

taken as written, then rearranged

clue.text: Third-rate minstrel and clumsy actor carrying extra weight?

heavier, more fat

clue.text: A ballerina not many forget dancing

blocks.note: these three words supply all the letters

explanation.definitionFit: Margot Fonteyn was a famous English ballerina, one of the greatest classical dancers of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Honours leader of expedition, extremely overweight

the opening letter of the word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like it signals the outer letters of 'expedition', but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese is the medical term for being very much heavier than a healthy weight.

the letters of these two words rearranged
ago means in the past

explanation.definitionFit: Chattanooga is a city in south-eastern Tennessee, known from the song Chattanooga Choo Choo.

clue.text: Discusses business lectures before small dance

blocks.note: a lecture is a talk
S is the abbreviation for small
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Someone talks business in lectures before heading off to a little dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is an idiom for discussing one's work or trade, especially at social occasions.

clue.text: Huge shortfall in fuel

explanation.definitionFit: Colossal and huge are synonyms, both meaning enormous, from the giant statue at Rhodes.

clue.text: Jazz pianist, Greek character, tired all the time, artist brought over

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist, a Greek character always worn out, brings an artist along.

explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was an American jazz pianist, famed for his dazzling technique.

clue.text: Victor's round?

clue.text: Affected, American university grounds

clue.text: Bring together in a religious service
